panels.narrative: The air in the Corridor of Alignment had thickened into something resembling a fluid. Jed Kramer moved through it with a heavy, rhythmic gait, his boots clicking against the polished concrete in time with the Tier-4 polyphonic drone emanating from the walls.

The scent of myrrh was no longer an olfactory glitch; it was a physical weight, cloying and ancient, masking the underlying sharp tang of ionized silicon. To his right, Sarah Chen walked with her tablet held like a shield.
The device’s screen was a frantic mess of scrolling logs, but the bezel was still weeping that same copper-smelling resin, staining her knuckles a dark, ceremonial red.
